title: Optimum bound from tester excess
statement: Let $q>0$, let $G$ be a regular unique game with alphabet of size $q$, and let its label set be nonempty. Suppose a finite set of sign predicates and real parameters $0<\alpha<\beta\le 1$ define a dictator-versus-no-influentials test family for every positive input dimension: its error function maps $[0,1]$ into $[0,1]$ and tends to $0$ as its argument decreases to $0$, every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$, and every function whose influences are all at most $\varepsilon$ is accepted with probability at most $\alpha+\mathrm{error}(\varepsilon)$. For any bounded long-code table $f$ for $G$, any $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, and any $\tau\in\mathbb R$, if the averaged-neighbor test value of $f$ is at least $\alpha+\mathrm{error}(\varepsilon)+\tau$, then the optimum value of the constraint satisfaction instance associated with $G$ is at least $\tau\varepsilon/(8q^2)$.
